seen_animation: A fixed line-drawn view down a bridge or pier: grey wall line at the horizon, two railings converging to a vanishing point, a vertical pole on the left and a lamp at top right. Black short slanted dashes fall as rain across the whole frame. Frames 1-4: sparse, evenly spread rain dashes and a small cluster of chevron splash marks at the bottom center of the deck. Frames 5-8: the rain thickens into a denser vertical column in the middle of the frame, and the splash marks grow into a band across the lower deck. Frames 9-12: the central column gets denser with longer strokes, splash marks spread over the whole visible deck, and in frames 11-12 a tight cluster of splash marks appears on the left near the railing. Frames 13-16: the densest rain, a heavy central curtain of long overlapping strokes reaching from the top of the frame to the deck, with splashes covering the deck and a left-side splash cluster again in frames 13 and 16.
seen_film: A static shot down a railed bridge or pier in rain, with a dark overhang at the top, a pole on the left and a lamp at top right. Frames 1-6: light fine rain, a small bright splash patch at the bottom center of the deck and a white line down the middle of the deck. Frames 7-9: the splashing on the deck widens across the lower deck. Frames 10-12: the rain darkens into a heavy central curtain, the whole deck is covered in splash glitter, and a patch of splashes appears on the left by the railing. Frames 13-16: the downpour stays heavy and dark in the center, the deck stays splashed, with the left-rail splash patch visible again in frame 16.
named_subject: Rain falling on a railed bridge or pier and splashing on its deck, drawn as short dash strokes with chevron splash marks.
evidence: Frames 1-4 in both show light rain with a small splash patch at bottom center. Frames 7-9 in both show the splashing spreading across the lower deck. Frames 11-12 in both show a splash cluster on the left near the railing (animation at left rail in 11-12, film in 10-12), and frame 16 repeats it in both. Frames 13-16 in both show a heavy central downpour reaching the deck. The scenery (railings, horizon wall, pole, lamp) stays fixed in the same positions as in the film across all 16 frames, and the rain strokes keep the doodle's short, slightly slanted, occasionally kinked dash form.
primary_gap: The rain thickens into a dense central column too early, by frames 5-6, while in the film the heavy dark curtain only builds from about frames 9-11, so the escalation leads the film by several frames.
closes_when: Frames 5-8 keep rain density close to frames 1-4 with only a slight central thickening, and the dense central column of long strokes first appears around frames 9-10 and peaks in 11-16.
protect: The fixed grey scenery matching the film's layout; the doodle's short slanted dash strokes as the rain unit; the bottom-center splash patch in frames 1-4; the left-rail splash cluster in frames 11-12 and 16; the steady spread of splash marks over the deck; no character drift or redraw of the scenery.
identity_gap: The rain uses the doodle's short slanted dashes, but in frames 13-16 many strokes become much longer than any in c.png and overlap into dark bundles, which moves away from the doodle's sparse, separated marks.
